title: The Ship That Wouldn't Sink
intro: This quiz follows Lila and Ben as they learn about buoyancy, density, and why large steel ships can float.

choices: The upward force that water exerts on an object
The amount of metal in an object
The speed at which an object moves
questions.explanation: Buoyancy is the upward force that water exerts on an object.

questions.prompt: Why did the lump of clay sink at first?
choices: It did not displace enough water to create a strong enough upward push
questions.explanation: The lump of clay sank because it did not displace enough water to create a strong enough upward push.

questions.prompt: Why did the same clay float after it was shaped like a small boat?
choices: It spread out and pushed aside more water
It changed into a different material
questions.explanation: The clay floated when shaped like a boat because it spread out and pushed aside more water.

questions.prompt: Why can a large steel ship float?
choices: Its wide, hollow shape gives it a lower average density and helps it displace a lot of water
Its engine holds it above the water
questions.explanation: A large steel ship can float because its wide, hollow shape gives it a lower average density and helps it displace a lot of water.

questions.prompt: Why can overloading a ship be dangerous?
choices: The ship may sink too low and lose its safe balance with the water's upward push
questions.explanation: Overloading a ship can be dangerous because it may sink too low and lose its safe balance with the water's upward push.
